judged_text: evt.destinationCalendar is initialized to null when neither eventType nor organizer has a destination calendar, which makes the later `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` a no-op that discards every member's collected destination calendar. Collective event types whose organizer uses the default primary calendar silently ignore all members' configured destination calendars, so members' calendars never receive the event — the precise gap the PR title claims to close.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts`, `evt.destinationCalendar` is set to `null` when neither `eventType.destinationCalendar` nor `organizerUser.destinationCalendar` exists (`destinationCalendar: ... : null`). Immediately after, for collective team events, the code does `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)`. Because `destinationCalendar` can be `null`, the optional-chained `push` becomes a no-op, dropping the collected `teamDestinationCalendars` entirely. This is directly verifiable from the diff and contradicts the intent of adding team members' destination calendars.
